headings.title: Rape crisis center employee confidentiality and notice obligations
headings.reviewNote: Covers rape crisis center duty to mandate confidentiality of identifying records and inform served individuals of confidentiality scope.

headings.title: Witness testimonial incompetence absent written client waiver
headings.reviewNote: Renders rape crisis center employees and volunteers incompetent to testify about subsection 1 confidential information unless waived in writing by the individual served; original-rolls footnote notes word "is" for "are".

headings.title: Rape crisis center defined
headings.reviewNote: Covers statutory definition of rape crisis center providing services to adult or qualified minor sexual assault victims.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 3 subsections against archived text including original-rolls footnote ("is" for "are" in subsection 2): rape crisis center confidentiality, testimonial incompetence absent written waiver, and definition.

headings.title: Filing verified petition for protection order
headings.reviewNote: Covers right of victims of domestic violence, stalking, or sexual assault to file a verified petition for an order of protection.

headings.title: Right to relief unimpaired by leaving residence
headings.reviewNote: Covers rule that leaving shared residence or household to escape abuse does not impair petitioner's right to statutory relief.

headings.title: Statewide effect of protection orders
headings.reviewNote: Covers statewide validity and enforceability of orders of protection in all Missouri cities and counties.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 3 subsections against archived text: verified protection-order petitions for domestic violence, stalking, or sexual assault, non-impairment by leaving residence, and statewide effect.

headings.title: Filing protection petition when court unavailable after hours
headings.reviewNote: Covers filing petitions before any available court in city or county after business hours, weekends, or holidays.

headings.title: Certification of after-hours filings to circuit court
headings.reviewNote: Covers clerk duty to certify after-hours petition filings and ex parte orders to circuit court on the next regular business day.

headings.title: Confidentiality of petitioner address and social security number
headings.reviewNote: Covers protection of petitioner residential address via in camera disclosure and prohibition on public social security number filing.

headings.title: Supreme court guidelines for after-hours petition filings
headings.reviewNote: Covers supreme court duty to establish guidelines ensuring availability of protection order filings on evenings, weekends, and holidays.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 4 subsections against archived text: after-hours/weekend/holiday filings, next-business-day circuit court certification, address and Social Security number confidentiality, and supreme court guidelines.

headings.title: Immediate ex parte protection order upon good cause shown
headings.reviewNote: Covers immediate issuance of ex parte order of protection upon showing immediate and present danger of domestic violence.

headings.title: Validity prior to service and service rules for minor respondents
headings.reviewNote: Covers validity of ex parte order prior to service, and service of process upon parent or guardian for minor respondents.

headings.title: Transfer to juvenile court and guardian ad litem for minor respondent
headings.reviewNote: Requires transferring the case to juvenile court for a full-order hearing when an ex parte order is entered against a respondent under age 17, and requires appointing a guardian ad litem if unrepresented by a parent or guardian.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified subsections 1 and 2 and corrected subsection 3 title/reviewNote (transfer to juvenile court and GAL appointment when respondent is under age 17, not child-allegation certification).

headings.title: Full order hearing timeframe, duration, and automatic renewal
headings.reviewNote: Requires a hearing within 15 days, sets full order duration at 180 days to 1 year (or 2 to 10 years, with renewals up to respondent's life, upon specific written findings of serious danger), covers automatic renewal, 7 danger factors, and a 2-year modification bar.

headings.title: Personal service of petition and notice of hearing
headings.reviewNote: Covers requirement of personal service of petition, hearing notice, and ex parte order on respondent at least three days prior to hearing.

headings.title: Distribution of orders and twenty-four-hour MULES and NCIC entry
headings.reviewNote: Requires issuing copies of orders to the petitioner and local law enforcement, sheriff entry into MULES within 24 hours (forwarding to NCIC/NICS, including custody/visitation specifics), expiration/termination notices, and optional automated court-to-MULES transfer.

headings.title: Personal service of respondent's automatic-renewal objection on petitioner
headings.reviewNote: Requires priority personal service on the petitioner of any respondent objection and hearing notice regarding automatic renewal of a one-year full order at least three days before the hearing.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified subsections 1 and 2 (expanding subsection 1 reviewNote to include 2–10 year/lifetime serious-danger orders and noting 1989 Ehrhart annotation) and replaced wrong headings in subsections 3 (MULES/NCIC 24-hour entry) and 4 (service of automatic-renewal objection).

headings.title: Permissible terms of full and ex parte protection orders
headings.reviewNote: Covers injunctive provisions restraining cyberstalking, abuse, molesting, residence exclusion, communication, and pet violence.

headings.title: Mutual orders of protection prohibited absent cross-petitions
headings.reviewNote: Covers statutory prohibition barring mutual orders of protection unless both parties file independent verified petitions with service.

headings.title: Ancillary relief in full order including custody, support, and property
headings.reviewNote: Covers additional relief upon full order including child custody, support, maintenance, mortgage payments, personal property, and counseling.

headings.title: Verified pleading requirements for financial and property relief
headings.reviewNote: Covers requirement that petitions specifically plead and pray for support, maintenance, rent, property possession, or shelter fees.

headings.title: Custody presumption favoring nonabusive parent
headings.reviewNote: Covers custody determination factors and rebuttable presumption that child custody with nonabusive parent serves best interests.

headings.title: Noncustodial parent visitation rights and guardian ad litem appointment
headings.reviewNote: Requires granting visitation to the noncustodial parent unless it endangers the child's physical health, impairs emotional development, conflicts with best interests, or cannot protect the custodial parent, and authorizes appointing a GAL or CASA.

headings.title: Child support order for noncustodial party
headings.reviewNote: Requires ordering the noncustodial party to pay reasonable and necessary child support under Supreme Court Rule 88.01 and chapter 452 when no prior support order is outstanding.

headings.title: Maintenance order up to one hundred eighty days
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a maintenance order to a party for up to 180 days in accordance with chapter 452.

headings.title: Transfer of wireless telephone billing responsibility and numbers
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes courts to order wireless service providers to transfer billing responsibility and wireless numbers to a non-accountholder petitioner, sets notice, 3-business-day inability notice, financial responsibility, provider immunity, and definition.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified subsections 1–5 (L. 2026 cyberstalking addition, severability/nonseverability cross-refs §§ 1.1005/1.1008) and replaced 4 completely hallucinated headings in subsections 6–9 (visitation, child support, 180-day maintenance, wireless billing transfer).

headings.title: Modification of full order of protection upon motion
headings.reviewNote: Covers modification of full protection orders upon written motion and hearing showing changed circumstances.

headings.title: Termination of ancillary orders upon subsequent statutory order
headings.reviewNote: Terminates child support, custody, temporary custody, visitation, or maintenance orders under sections 455.010 to 455.085 upon issuance of a subsequent order under chapter 452 or another Missouri statute.

headings.title: Orders not res judicata in subsequent proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Provides that no order entered under sections 455.010 to 455.085 is res judicata to any subsequent proceeding, including chapter 452 actions.

headings.title: Termination upon dissolution or legal separation with exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Terminates all protection order provisions upon entry of a dissolution or legal separation decree, except counseling, anti-domestic-violence injunctions, and dwelling exclusion while petitioner resides there unless respondent is awarded possession.

headings.title: Termination upon petitioner's motion and voluntary-dismissal inquiry
headings.reviewNote: Terminates protection or ancillary orders upon court approval of the petitioner's motion to terminate, permitting court inquiry into whether dismissal is voluntary.

headings.title: Prohibition on changing child custody during dissolution or prior award
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits a protection order from changing child custody when a dissolution action has been filed or custody was previously awarded by a court of competent jurisdiction.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified subsection 1 and replaced 5 shifted/hallucinated draft headings in subsections 2–6 (early termination of ancillary orders, non-res-judicata, dissolution termination with exceptions, petitioner termination motion, and custody-change prohibition).

headings.title: Modification of maintenance or support orders on changed circumstances
headings.reviewNote: Limits modification of maintenance or support provisions to subsequent installments upon a showing of substantial and continuing changed circumstances making the terms unreasonable.

headings.title: Modification of custody orders based on new facts and best interests
headings.reviewNote: Allows modification of custody provisions only upon new or previously unknown facts showing a change in circumstances of the child or custodian and necessity for the child's best interests.

headings.title: Modification of visitation orders in child's best interests
headings.reviewNote: Permits modification of visitation provisions whenever modification would serve the child's best interests.

entries.reviewSummary: Replaced all 3 completely hallucinated draft headings with source-bound headings for modification of maintenance/support, custody, and visitation orders.

headings.title: Full faith and credit for foreign orders of protection
headings.reviewNote: Covers statutory mandate granting full faith and credit and interstate enforceability to valid foreign protection orders.

headings.title: Registration of foreign protection orders with circuit court
headings.reviewNote: Covers procedure for filing and registering certified copies of foreign protection orders with circuit court clerks.

headings.title: Filing of foreign protection orders without fee or cost
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that filing a foreign order of protection be without fee or cost.

headings.title: Law enforcement enforcement of unregistered foreign orders
headings.reviewNote: Covers law enforcement authority to enforce foreign protection orders upon verification of validity without prior Missouri registration.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified subsections 1, 2, and 4 and replaced hallucinated subsection 3 heading (filing foreign protection orders without fee or cost, not law enforcement database entry).

headings.title: Supreme court adoption of uniform protection order forms
headings.reviewNote: Covers supreme court duty to adopt standard simplified forms and instructions for domestic violence protection petitions and orders.

headings.title: Required boldface or capital-letter warnings on protection orders
headings.reviewNote: Requires boldface or all-caps warnings on protection orders stating potential penalties (up to 5 years jail and $5,000 fine) and dwelling exclusion if ordered.

headings.title: Required notice of potential relief and default on hearing form
headings.reviewNote: Requires the supreme court's section 455.040(2) hearing notice form to list all potential section 455.050 relief and advise the respondent that relief may be granted on finding for petitioner or default.

headings.title: Continuation of temporary orders within full order of protection
headings.reviewNote: Continues all temporary orders within a granted full order of protection unless otherwise ordered by the court.

headings.title: Mandatory issuance of protection orders on uniform supreme court form
headings.reviewNote: Requires all orders of protection to be issued on the uniform form adopted under subsection 1.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified subsection 1 and replaced 4 completely hallucinated draft headings in subsections 2–5 (boldface warnings, hearing-notice relief/default disclosures, continuation of temporary orders, and mandatory uniform form).

headings.title: Law enforcement recordkeeping and verification of prior abuse
headings.reviewNote: Covers law enforcement establishment of central records to track domestic violence incidents and verify effective protection orders.

headings.title: Standard of law enforcement response and priority dispatch factors
headings.reviewNote: Covers prohibition against deprioritizing domestic calls compared to stranger offenses and factors mandating immediate response.

headings.title: Domestic crisis intervention teams and specialized officers
headings.reviewNote: Covers authorization for law enforcement agencies to deploy crisis intervention teams, counseling specialists, and trained officers.

headings.title: Officer duty to inform victim of legal remedies and shelter services
headings.reviewNote: Covers officer duty at scene of abuse to provide notice of available legal remedies, judicial relief, and emergency shelters.

headings.title: Officer arrangement of emergency transportation for medical care or shelter
headings.reviewNote: Covers officer duty to provide or arrange transportation for abused parties to medical treatment facilities or emergency shelters.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 5 subsections against archived text: law enforcement records, equal response standard and immediate-response factors, crisis teams, victim remedy/shelter notice, and emergency transportation.

headings.title: Domestic violence warrantless arrest, nonarrest report, and twelve-hour rule
headings.reviewNote: Permits warrantless arrest on probable cause of domestic violence against a family or household member, requires a written report if declining arrest, mandates arrest on a second call within 12 hours, and disregards victim refusal to sign a complaint.

headings.title: Mandatory warrantless arrest for abuse violating protective order
headings.reviewNote: Mandates warrantless arrest when an officer has probable cause that a respondent with notice of a protective order committed an act of abuse violating the order, regardless of victim refusal to sign a complaint.

headings.title: Primary physical aggressor determination and dual arrest prohibition
headings.reviewNote: Covers evaluation factors for identifying primary physical aggressor and prohibition against dual arrest threats to discourage calls.

headings.title: Officer and agency immunity for good-faith domestic violence arrests
headings.reviewNote: Covers civil immunity protecting law enforcement officers and employing agencies from false arrest or malicious prosecution claims.

headings.title: Mandatory arrest and custody transfer for child custody violations
headings.reviewNote: Covers officer duty to arrest respondents refusing to surrender minor children awarded in protection order and transfer custody.

headings.title: Constitutional detention protections applicable to arrested respondent
headings.reviewNote: Covers application of standard constitutional safeguards and detention procedures to respondents arrested under section 455.085.

headings.title: Criminal penalties for violation of ex parte order of protection
headings.reviewNote: Covers classification of ex parte order violation as class A misdemeanor, elevated to class E felony for prior conviction in 5 years.

headings.title: Criminal penalties for violation of full order of protection
headings.reviewNote: Covers classification of full order violation as class A misdemeanor or class E felony, and constructive notice by officer presentation.

headings.title: Good-faith marital reconciliation attempts not witness tampering
headings.reviewNote: Covers protection ensuring good-faith marital reconciliation attempts are not prosecuted as witness or victim tampering.

headings.title: No private right of action created
headings.reviewNote: Covers express statutory limitation clarifying that section 455.085 does not create a private civil cause of action for damages.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified subsections 3–10 (noting 1982 Williams v. Marsh and 1996 Schleiermacher annotations) and corrected swapped headings in subsections 1 (domestic violence warrantless arrest/12-hour rule) and 2 (mandatory arrest for protective order abuse violation).

headings.title: Retained jurisdiction and compliance review hearings
headings.reviewNote: Covers court retention of jurisdiction over full protection orders and scheduling compliance review hearings to monitor obedience.

headings.title: Judgment enforcement remedies and judicial contempt sanctions
headings.reviewNote: Covers enforcement of protection order terms via standard judgment remedies and judicial punishment of willful violations as contempt.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified both subsections against archived text: retained court jurisdiction with compliance review hearings, and judgment enforcement remedies with willful-violation contempt sanctions.

headings.title: Definitions for electronic monitoring with victim notification
headings.reviewNote: Covers definitions for electronic monitoring with victim notification and eight informed consent requirements for protected persons.

headings.title: Electronic monitoring ordered upon conviction or probation condition
headings.reviewNote: Covers court authority to impose electronic monitoring with victim notification upon conviction or as probation condition.

headings.title: Pretrial release condition ordering electronic monitoring
headings.reviewNote: Covers judicial authority to order electronic monitoring with victim notification as a condition of pretrial release under section 544.455.

headings.title: Mandatory informed consent and judicial evaluation factors
headings.reviewNote: Covers requirement of victim informed consent and seven statutory factors considered at hearing before ordering electronic monitoring.

headings.title: Payment of monitoring costs by defendant absent indigency
headings.reviewNote: Covers defendant responsibility to pay costs of electronic monitoring equipment and services unless found indigent by court.

headings.title: Monitoring alert as probable cause for warrantless arrest
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that an alert from an electronic monitoring device constitutes probable cause to arrest the monitored person for violating an ex parte or full order of protection.

headings.title: Interagency sharing of electronic monitoring information
headings.reviewNote: Requires the departments of corrections and public safety, state highway patrol, circuit courts, and local law enforcement agencies to share electronic monitoring information obtained under section 455.095.

headings.title: Supplier liability immunity except for manufacturing defects
headings.reviewNote: Shields suppliers of electronic monitoring products, systems, or services from direct or indirect injury or death damages except to the extent proximately caused by a manufacturing defect.

headings.title: Court authority for monitoring without victim notification preserved
headings.reviewNote: Preserves court authority to order electronic monitoring without victim notification under section 544.455 or 557.011.

headings.title: Tampering with ordered electronic monitoring equipment offense
headings.reviewNote: Subjects a person who commits prohibited tampering acts with court-ordered monitoring equipment under section 455.095 to the offense of tampering under section 575.205.

headings.title: Department of corrections rulemaking and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department of corrections to promulgate rules implementing subsection 5 under chapter 536 and section 536.028, with a post-August 28, 2018 nonseverability clause.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified subsections 1–5 (A.L. 2025 H.B. 495, § 1.1001 severability) and replaced 6 completely hallucinated/shifted headings in subsections 6–11 (probable cause alert, interagency sharing, supplier defect-only liability, non-notification monitoring, § 575.205 tampering, and DOC rulemaking/nonseverability).

headings.title: Lifetime protection order at dangerous-felony sentencing and termination
headings.reviewNote: Grants sentencing courts jurisdiction, on victim or prosecutor request, to enter an immediately effective lifetime protection order upon a section 556.061 dangerous-felony conviction, terminating only upon victim death/dismissal/expungement/reversal/pardon or victim's written request.

headings.title: Distribution of lifetime orders and twenty-four-hour MULES entry
headings.reviewNote: Requires issuing copies of lifetime protection orders to the victim and local law enforcement, sheriff entry into MULES within 24 hours (forwarding to NCIC/NICS), termination notices, and optional automated data transfer.

entries.reviewSummary: Replaced both completely hallucinated draft headings (which erroneously described remote video appearances) with source-bound headings for L. 2026 lifetime protection orders at dangerous-felony sentencing and 24-hour MULES/NCIC entry.

headings.title: Application for county domestic violence shelter funding
headings.reviewNote: Covers procedure for eligible domestic violence shelters to apply for county shelter funds derived from marriage license surcharges.

headings.title: November 15 written eligibility notice and available funding amount
headings.reviewNote: Requires the designated authority by November 15 to notify qualifying shelters in writing of eligibility and available funding from fees collected under section 455.205 (source footnote: transferred to section 488.445 in 2000).

headings.title: Semiannual payment of allocated shelter funds in January and July
headings.reviewNote: Requires semiannual payment of allocated shelter funds on January 1 and July 1 of the year following application.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified subsection 1 and replaced inaccurate draft headings in subsections 2 (Nov 15 eligibility/funding notice; noted § 455.205 transfer to § 488.445) and 3 (semiannual Jan 1 / Jul 1 payments).

headings.title: Six statutory requirements for shelters to qualify for funds
headings.reviewNote: Lists six mandatory qualification criteria for section 455.215 shelter funding: nonprofit incorporation, diverse trustees including lived experience, 25% outside funding, residential services for accompanied children, confidentiality, and confidentiality notice.

headings.title: Testimonial incompetence of shelter personnel absent written waiver
headings.reviewNote: Renders shelter employees and volunteers incompetent to testify concerning subsection 1(5) confidential information unless waived in writing by the individual served.

headings.title: Disqualification for discriminatory admissions or service practices
headings.reviewNote: Disqualifies shelters that discriminate in admissions or services based on race, religion, color, age, marital status, national origin, or ancestry.

entries.reviewSummary: Replaced all 3 completely wrong draft headings (confused with § 455.230) with source-bound headings for six shelter qualification requirements, personnel testimonial incompetence, and nondiscrimination; noted 2004 Hope House v. Merrigan annotation.

headings.title: Annual March 31 shelter reports, anonymity, and renovation grants
headings.reviewNote: Requires funded shelters to file annual reports by March 31 with service statistics and independent audit results without identifying victims, and authorizes 75/25 state/local DPS renovation and construction grants subject to appropriation.

headings.title: Annual compilation of shelter reports by designated authority
headings.reviewNote: Directs the designated authority to annually compile the shelter reports filed under subsection 1.

headings.title: Department of social services funding for child assessment center
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department of social services, subject to appropriation, to fund a child assessment center in qualifying non-charter first-classification counties (population 160,000–200,000).

entries.reviewSummary: Replaced all 3 completely hallucinated draft headings (which erroneously described tax credits) with source-bound headings for March 31 annual reports/renovation grants, annual compilation, and DSS child assessment center funding.

headings.title: Establishment and composition of Missouri Domestic Violence Commission
headings.reviewNote: Covers creation of Missouri Domestic Violence Commission within Department of Public Safety and appointment of judicial and public members.

headings.title: Open public meetings schedule and legislative notice
headings.reviewNote: Covers sunshine law compliance, bi-monthly meeting requirement, and mandatory public notice to the general assembly.

headings.title: Commission procedural rulemaking authority
headings.reviewNote: Covers commission authority to adopt internal procedural rules for meetings, officer elections, and operating guidelines.

headings.title: Election of commission officers
headings.reviewNote: Covers commission election of chairman, vice chairman, secretary-reporter, and other necessary officers from membership.

headings.title: Department staff assistance and in-state meeting requirement
headings.reviewNote: Covers availability of department agency staff to assist commission and mandate that all commission meetings be held within Missouri.

headings.title: Appointment and role of non-voting ex officio members
headings.reviewNote: Covers commission authority to invite non-voting ex officio members from local, federal, or private agencies with expense reimbursement.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 6 subsections against archived text: Missouri Domestic Violence Commission composition, open meetings, procedural rules, officers, agency staff/in-state meetings, and non-voting ex officio members.

headings.title: Establishment and purposes of intervention and rehabilitation pilot projects
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department of social services and domestic violence commission beginning in 2001 to establish up to 20 satellite domestic violence intervention/rehabilitation pilot projects for four enumerated purposes.

headings.title: Pilot program funding subject to appropriation
headings.reviewNote: Makes funding for the domestic violence pilot programs subject to appropriation.

headings.title: Administrative rulemaking authority and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Directs chapter 536 rulemaking by the department and commission with a post-August 28, 2000 nonseverability clause (archived text contains typo "to dely").

headings.title: Annual report of activities to governor and general assembly
headings.reviewNote: Covers requirement that department and commission submit annual activity reports to legislative leaders and governor by December 31.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified subsections 3 (noting archived typo "to dely") and 4, and replaced wrong draft headings in subsections 1 (up to 20 intervention/rehabilitation pilot projects) and 2 (funding subject to appropriation).

headings.title: Venue for child protection order petitions
headings.reviewNote: Covers venue in county where child resides, where abuse or stalking occurred, or where respondent may be served.

headings.title: Persons authorized to file child protection petition
headings.reviewNote: Covers standing to file child protection petitions by parents, guardians, guardians ad litem, CASA volunteers, or juvenile officers.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified both subsections against archived text: venue for child protection order petitions and authorized filers (parent/guardian, GAL/CASA, juvenile officer).

headings.title: Court clerk assistance for child protection petitions without fees
headings.reviewNote: Covers clerk duty to provide child protection forms, explain procedures without legal fees, and post conspicuous assistance notices.

headings.title: No filing fees or costs assessed to child protection petitioner
headings.reviewNote: Covers prohibition against assessing filing fees, court costs, or bond requirements in child protection order actions.

headings.title: Clerk notification of guardian ad litem appointment
headings.reviewNote: Covers clerk duty to provide immediate notice of appointment and party contact information to guardian ad litem or advocate within 24 hours.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 3 subsections against archived text: clerk uniform forms and pro se assistance without cost, no petitioner fees/costs/bond, and 24-hour GAL/CASA appointment notice.

headings.title: Verified petition for child protection order
headings.reviewNote: Covers filing verified petition for child protection order alleging domestic violence, sexual assault, or stalking against a minor.

headings.title: Child's right to relief unimpaired by leaving residence
headings.reviewNote: Covers rule that child's departure from residence to avoid domestic violence does not affect entitlement to statutory protection.

headings.title: Statewide effect of child protection orders
headings.reviewNote: Covers statewide validity and enforceability of child orders of protection across all Missouri cities and counties.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 3 subsections against archived text: verified child protection petitions, non-impairment by leaving residence, and statewide effect.

headings.title: After-hours child protection petition filings
headings.reviewNote: Covers filing child protection petitions before any available court in city or county when court is closed for business.

headings.title: Next business day certification of child petitions to circuit court
headings.reviewNote: Covers court clerk duty to certify after-hours child protection filings and orders to circuit court on the next regular business day.

headings.title: Confidentiality of child residence and address
headings.reviewNote: Covers protection of child residence via in camera disclosure and exception allowing withholding mailing address for child safety.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 3 subsections against archived text (effective 5-15-96): after-hours child protection filings, next-business-day circuit court certification, and child address confidentiality.

headings.title: Ex parte child protection order upon immediate danger
headings.reviewNote: Covers immediate issuance of ex parte child protection order upon showing danger of abuse, sexual assault, stalking, or pet harm.

headings.title: Mandatory appointment of guardian ad litem or advocate
headings.reviewNote: Covers court duty to enter order appointing guardian ad litem or court-appointed special advocate upon entering ex parte child order.

headings.title: Children's division investigation and thirty-day report
headings.reviewNote: Covers court referral to children's division for investigation and services, with 30-day written report to court and juvenile officer.

headings.title: Transfer to juvenile court when respondent is under seventeen
headings.reviewNote: Covers issuance of ex parte order and mandatory transfer of case to juvenile court for hearing when respondent is under age seventeen.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 4 subsections against archived text: immediate ex parte child protection orders, mandatory GAL/CASA appointment, 30-day children's division investigation, and juvenile court transfer for respondents under age 17.

headings.title: Hearing timeframe, full order duration, and child evidence rules
headings.reviewNote: Covers 15-day hearing, closed hearing discretion, videotape/child statement admissibility, order duration, and renewal without new abuse.

headings.title: Personal service of petition and child protection hearing notice
headings.reviewNote: Covers requirement of personal service of petition, hearing notice, and ex parte order on respondent at least three days prior to hearing.

headings.title: Order distribution to petitioner, law enforcement, and MULES entry
headings.reviewNote: Requires issuing child protection orders to the petitioner, local law enforcement, and same-day to the MULES-maintaining agency for 24-hour MULES entry, plus expiration/termination notices and optional automated data transfer.

headings.title: Distribution of child protection petitions and orders to juvenile office
headings.reviewNote: Requires issuing copies of the petition, hearing notice, child protection order, and expiration/termination notices to the juvenile office where the petitioner resides.

headings.title: Personal service of respondent's automatic-renewal objection on petitioner
headings.reviewNote: Requires priority personal service on the petitioner of any respondent objection and hearing notice regarding automatic renewal of a one-year full child protection order at least three days before the hearing.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified subsections 1 and 2 and replaced 3 completely wrong draft headings in subsections 3 (order distribution/24-hour MULES entry), 4 (juvenile office copies), and 5 (personal service of automatic-renewal objection on petitioner).

headings.title: Permissible relief in ex parte child protection orders
headings.reviewNote: Covers ex parte terms restraining respondent from abusing child, entering school or dwelling, communicating, or harming pets.

headings.title: Required findings for ex parte exclusion from family home
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits an ex parte child protection order excluding the respondent from the family home unless the court finds best interests of remaining children, substantial risk of domestic violence, and an able remaining adult caretaker.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified subsection 1 and replaced wrong subsection 2 heading (three required findings for ex parte family-home exclusion, not custody awards).

headings.title: Permissible injunctive terms in full child protection orders
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes full child protection order injunctive terms protecting the victim (and child's pet) from domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, molesting, disturbing the peace, family-home entry, and communication.

headings.title: Ancillary custody, support, treatment, wireless, and pet relief
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes ten ancillary remedies in full child protection orders: custody, visitation, child support, maintenance, rent/mortgage payments, counseling, treatment costs, shelter fees, section 455.050(9) wireless number transfer for minor children, and pet possession/vet costs.

entries.reviewSummary: Revised both subsection headings to accurately separate subsection 1 injunctive terms from subsection 2 ancillary relief (custody, support, treatment, wireless transfer, and pets; removed unstated attorney fees).

headings.title: Retained court jurisdiction and compliance review hearings
headings.reviewNote: Retains court jurisdiction over full child protection orders for their entire duration and permits scheduling compliance review hearings.

headings.title: Judgment enforcement remedies and contempt sanctions for violations
headings.reviewNote: Makes child protection order terms enforceable by all judgment remedies and authorizes contempt punishment for willful violations.

entries.reviewSummary: Replaced both completely hallucinated draft headings (which erroneously described CASA) with source-bound headings for retained jurisdiction/compliance review hearings and judgment/contempt enforcement.

headings.title: Child protection order modification upon motion and hearing
headings.reviewNote: Covers modification of full child protection orders upon written motion and hearing showing substantial changed circumstances.

headings.title: Termination of ancillary orders upon subsequent statutory order
headings.reviewNote: Terminates child support, custody, temporary custody, visitation, or maintenance orders under sections 455.500 to 455.538 upon issuance of a subsequent order under chapter 452 or another Missouri statute.

headings.title: Orders not res judicata in subsequent proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Provides that no order entered under sections 455.500 to 455.538 is res judicata to any subsequent proceeding, including chapter 452 actions.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified subsection 1 and replaced wrong draft headings in subsections 2 (termination of ancillary orders upon subsequent statutory order) and 3 (orders not res judicata).

headings.title: Modification of maintenance or support orders on changed circumstances
headings.reviewNote: Limits modification of maintenance or support provisions to subsequent installments upon a showing of substantial and continuing changed circumstances making the terms unreasonable.

headings.title: Modification of custody orders based on new facts and best interests
headings.reviewNote: Allows modification of custody provisions only upon new or previously unknown facts showing a change in circumstances of the child or custodian and necessity for the child's best interests.

headings.title: Modification of visitation orders in child's best interests
headings.reviewNote: Permits modification of visitation provisions whenever modification would serve the child's best interests.

entries.reviewSummary: Replaced all 3 completely hallucinated draft headings with source-bound headings for modification of maintenance/support, custody, and visitation orders.

headings.title: Warrantless arrest authority for child protection order violation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes warrantless arrest when a law enforcement officer has probable cause that a respondent violated a child protection order, whether or not committed in the officer's presence.

headings.title: Mandatory arrest and custody transfer for child custody violations
headings.reviewNote: Mandates arresting a respondent who fails to surrender minor children awarded in a child protection order and turning the children over to the awarded custodian.

headings.title: Constitutional detention procedures applicable to arrested respondent
headings.reviewNote: Requires applying the same detention procedures, including constitutional-rights protections, to an arrested respondent as to any other person in police custody.

headings.title: Criminal penalties for violation and officer-presented notice
headings.reviewNote: Classifies violation of an ex parte or full child protection order as a class A misdemeanor (or class E felony with a prior conviction within 5 years, court-sentenced) and deems respondent to have notice when a responding officer presents a copy.

headings.title: Prosecution for other crimes arising from incident preserved
headings.reviewNote: Preserves prosecution of a respondent for other crimes arising out of the same incident in which a child protection order is alleged to have been violated.

entries.reviewSummary: Replaced all 5 shifted/hallucinated draft headings with source-bound headings for warrantless arrest, mandatory custody-violation arrest/transfer, constitutional detention procedures, criminal penalties/notice, and preservation of other prosecutions.

headings.title: Law enforcement determination of domestic violence in homicides or suicides
headings.reviewNote: Requires law enforcement agencies investigating any homicide or suicide to determine whether it is related to domestic violence.

headings.title: Factors considered in domestic violence determination
headings.reviewNote: Lists four permissive factors law enforcement agencies may consider in determining domestic-violence relation: family/household relationship, prior protection order filings, prior domestic violence investigations, and other evidence.

headings.title: Highway patrol development and distribution of reporting form
headings.reviewNote: Covers state highway patrol duty to develop and distribute standardized reporting forms to all state law enforcement agencies.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified subsection 3 and replaced wrong/shifted draft headings in subsections 1 (domestic-violence determination in homicides or suicides) and 2 (four permissive determination factors).

headings.title: Division of probation and parole standards for batterer intervention
headings.reviewNote: Covers division of probation and parole duty to promulgate standards and credentialing processes for court-appointed batterer programs.

headings.title: Administrative rulemaking authority and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Covers division administrative rulemaking authority under chapter 536 and legislative disapproval nonseverability clause.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified both subsections against archived text: division of probation and parole batterer intervention standards/credentialing and chapter 536 rulemaking compliance/nonseverability.

headings.title: Prosecuting attorney authority to impanel domestic violence fatality panel
headings.reviewNote: Covers prosecutor or circuit attorney authority to impanel local fatality review panel to investigate domestic violence homicides.

headings.title: Multidisciplinary membership of fatality review panel
headings.reviewNote: Covers mandatory panel composition including prosecutors, coroners, law enforcement, healthcare providers, and domestic violence advocates.

headings.title: Organization, chairperson election, and convening of panel
headings.reviewNote: Covers panel organization by prosecuting attorney, election of chairperson, and convening meetings to review domestic fatalities.

headings.title: Municipal and county requests to convene fatality panel
headings.reviewNote: Covers authority of municipal and county executive officers to request convening fatality review panel for local domestic deaths.

headings.title: Confidentiality and evidentiary privilege of panel work products
headings.reviewNote: Covers non-public record status and evidentiary inadmissibility of panel investigatory materials, summaries, and records.

headings.title: Final report as public record and distribution to state leaders
headings.reviewNote: Covers requirement that panel issue public final report with findings, recommendations, and summary distributed to state leaders.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 6 subsections against archived text: domestic violence fatality review panel impaneling, multidisciplinary membership, organization, municipal/county requests, work-product confidentiality, and public final report distribution.
